name: Es Cucons
open: Open until 15 Nov · reopens end of February
desc: Rural hotel in a 17th-century finca on the Pla de Corona, with a spa, sauna, hot tub, restaurant and live concerts. Closes mid-November and reopens at the end of February, just as the almond blossom fades — the Santa Agnès address for a late-winter weekend.

name: Las Puertas del Cielo
open: Open until 15 Nov · reopens end of February
desc: Clifftop bar-restaurant above the north-west coast, named for the 'gates of heaven' view. One of the island's great sunset spots and the natural end to the Ses Balandres walk. Closes 15 November, back at the end of February.

name: Can Cosmi
desc: The village bar-restaurant opposite the church: the island's most talked-about tortilla, lamb chops, rustic salads and a terrace in the sun. Salsa nights in winter — ask at the bar for the next one.
now: Live music at dinner some nights — blues, a guitar, whoever's on the island — 20:00–22:00, announced the same day on @cancosmi. Salsa nights too; ask at the bar.

name: Sa Palmera
desc: Classic Spanish cooking on the village square — the locals' choice after a walk. Simple, honest plates and a terrace that catches the winter sun.

name: Ses Casetes Art Café
desc: Country restaurant on the square in Es Pla de Sant Mateu: homemade island cooking, grilled meats and fish, a riot of colour inside, art on every wall and live concerts. Lunch in the winter sun after a walk through the Albarca vineyards. Open all year — book on WhatsApp.
ppp: Want it done for you? We'll set up your birthday or private table here — chef's menu, music, the guest list.

name: Juntos House
desc: Farmhouse restaurant, shop and clubhouse: organic plates from their own land, natural wines and cocktails, plus The Pergola for walk-in drinks and tapas. Open through the holidays last winter — check their Instagram for current days.

name: Mercat de Forada — Can Tixedó
desc: The island's most local Saturday market, in the field by Can Tixedó Art Café: farm fruit and veg, homemade food, crafts, a book swap, kids' zone, vegan paella at 13:00 and the odd live set. Coffee and lunch at Tixedó afterwards.

name: La Finca Can Suldat
desc: Swiss-Ibizan finca restaurant under a vine-roofed courtyard: cheese fondue, steak, goulash and 'Peter's famous salad', with live music through the winter. Go early evening to catch the music with the locals, and book a table.

name: Es Pins Cala Pada
village: Cala Pada, Es Canar · Santa Eulària
desc: Since 1976, hidden among the pines above Cala Pada on the Es Canar road (km 3.1): island flavours from a wood-fired kitchen, breakfasts and long lunches under the trees, and live music at the weekend. Mains from about €10 — one of the old-school beach restaurants that stays open when the resort around it has gone quiet. A children's corner is coming.

name: La Paloma
desc: An old finca among orange and lemon trees, with lunch in the flowering garden and dinners by lantern light: Italian-meets-Middle-Eastern plates, homemade bread, organic salads and a good bottle. Hours shift with the season — check their Instagram before you drive out.

name: Bar Costa
open: Open all year except March · closed Tuesdays
desc: The village institution on the square, hams hanging from the ceiling and paintings left by artists who paid in canvases. Bocadillos, tostadas and a cortado at the bar — the place the whole island passes through on a winter Sunday.

name: Bar Anita
desc: The hippie-era village bar opposite the church, with the old wooden post boxes still on the wall. Home-made hierbas, simple plates, a shaded terrace — and open every single day of the year.

name: Bar Can Berri
desc: Tiny bar on the prettiest village square in the west, under the church. Known in winter for its calçotades on Sundays in February and March: charred spring onions, romesco, grilled meat and plenty of wine.

name: Sa Carboneria
desc: Steakhouse and garden just behind the town hall: aged meats over charcoal, a warm dining room for the cold nights, a small garden for the sunny lunches. Winter weekends bring the Hunger BBQ, and Sa Carbo Bar has live music October to March — this is where The Oyster Nomad set up in October.

name: The Oyster Nomad
open: All winter · delivers and pops up
desc: A travelling oysterman — top hat, shucking knives, Umami oysters and AIX rosé — who delivers to villas and restaurants across the island all winter and shows up for pop-up nights. Shuck the world. No bar, no terrace: he comes to you.

name: Olas Gallery
desc: Photographer Sofia Gómez Fonzo's gallery and concept store a few steps from the beach: a show that changes every month, always with island artists — painting, aerial and underwater photography, cyanotypes, hand-stitched maps — and a shelf of books, prints, ceramics and oracle cards made on Ibiza. Talks and openings through the winter.
now: Autumn programme: Marcel Boer's Ibiza light studies, then Arnoud L∆L∆, and a group show of island artists in December.

name: Parra & Romero
desc: The Madrid gallery's island outpost in an industrial space on the village paseo: conceptual and minimal art, site-specific projects, the kind of show you'd expect in Chelsea, with a coffee at Bar Costa afterwards. Tue–Sat 11–14 & 16:30–20:30, Mondays 17–21.
now: Landon Metz — the Arizona painter's first solo show in Spain, opened late September.

name: MACE — Museu d'Art Contemporani
desc: One of Spain's first contemporary art museums, set into the walls of Dalt Vila with the Phoenician and Roman foundations visible under glass floors. The permanent collection is the island's art story since the 1960s; the temporary shows are the reason to go back. Winter hours: Tue–Fri 10–16:30, weekends 10–14.

name: Es Polvorí
desc: The old gunpowder store on the Santa Llúcia bastion, now the town's space for temporary shows: painting, photography and sculpture by artists living here, in a vaulted stone room with the harbour below. Tue–Fri 18–20:30, weekends 11–13:30.

name: Galería Marta Torres
desc: A gallery in the port since the 1990s: Marta Torres's own work and group shows of island painters, part of the emerging art route around La Marina. Mon–Fri 10–14.

name: Can Curt
desc: The village exhibition room opposite the church — painting, photography, sculpture, mostly by people who live within ten minutes of it. Combine with a drink at Can Berri Vell across the square. Thu–Sun 18–21.

name: Can Jeroni
desc: Sant Josep's cultural centre: exhibitions downstairs, and through the winter a programme of film, poetry, concerts and theatre that the village actually turns up for. Wed–Sun 10:30–13:30, plus Thu–Sat 18–21.

name: Sa Punta des Molí
desc: A restored windmill and olive press on the bay, with an exhibition hall and an open-air auditorium. Small shows by local artists; worth the walk along the promenade on a bright winter morning. Winter: Tuesdays and Saturdays 10–13 & 16–19.

name: Bartienne & The Cook's Atelier
open: All winter · dinners twice a month
desc: Barbara and Etienne's antique and interiors shop on the Santa Eulària road — French flea-market furniture, pieces from Asia and India, outdoor kitchens — with an open kitchen at the back. Barbara cooks there: long-table dinners for 20 to 40 a couple of weekends a month, and cooking workshops (Spanish, Italian, French) for groups. Follow @the_cooks_atelier_ibiza for the next date, or book the whole space for your own night. Carretera Santa Eulària 380.

name: Chez Bibi
desc: Café-restaurant with its own little bakery at the top of the village: Parisian croissants and cinnamon rolls, sourdough, poke and big salads, cakes that change daily. Laptops are welcome — on a grey winter morning half the terrace is working, the other half is on its second coffee. Dog-friendly, card accepted, book for lunch at weekends.

name: Es Vermell Cafè
village: Carrer del Bisbe Abad y Lasierra, Ibiza Town
desc: The town's own breakfast bar: loud, fast, cheap, full of people who work round the corner. Tostada, café con leche, done.

name: Es Tap Nou
desc: Juices pressed in front of you and a ham tostada on the open terrace in the shopping streets — the breakfast before the Saturday errands.

name: Croissant Show
village: At the foot of the Dalt Vila drawbridge, Ibiza Town
desc: Since the 1980s: croissants with serrano at the tables under the walls, the whole port walking past. Winter sun hits the terrace mid-morning.

name: Bar Can Toni
village: Ca Na Negreta, on the Santa Eulària road
desc: A roadside bar with a terrace and parking: tostadas, bocadillos, workmen's prices. Sa Barda next door is the same idea.

name: Can Rei
desc: The village café with homemade everything and km-0 produce, run by people who remember your order. Breakfast before the walk to the port.

name: Bar Cruce
desc: The bar at the crossroads where half the island stops for a coffee and a tostada on the way to work. No menu in English, no need.

name: Racó Verd
desc: A patio behind the main street with a Mexican-leaning breakfast and Spanish standards, good prices, and live music nights through the winter.

name: La Guay
desc: Churros made fresh, strong coffee, the regulars at the bar. Sant Antoni's local breakfast.

name: Can Guillem
village: Roadside at the Sant Agustí turn-off
desc: An old roadside bar nobody tells tourists about: jamón serrano and manchego on toast, a coffee, the lorries going past.

name: Cool Café
desc: Open before anyone else on the bay: tostadas, tortilla, coffee and juice for the dawn-walk crowd.

name: Hostal Talamanca
desc: Faces east, so breakfast here is in the sun from the first light. Tostada with sobrassada and two cheeses, feet almost in the sand.

name: Massa Coffee
desc: Specialist coffee done properly, pastries and a few savoury plates, on the walk from the port to Talamanca.

name: Forn Can Bufí
desc: The island's bakery: ensaimadas, magdalenas, flaó, orelletes and real bread. Buy the breakfast and take it to the beach.

name: Restaurante Pou des Lleó
open: Open all year except December · lunch 13:00–16:30, dinner 19:30–22:30
desc: The fishermen's cove below Sant Carles, with the old boat huts and a restaurant a few metres from the water. Bullit de peix, arròs a banda with alioli and paella from the wood fire — the kind of place islanders drive to on a Sunday, not the tourist list. Closes only for December.

name: Port Balansat
open: Open until the end of November · reduced winter days — call ahead
desc: Right on the beach at Port de Sant Miquel and, by island consensus, one of the best fish restaurants on Ibiza — the first to put bullit de peix on a menu. Fresh, boneless, no fuss. Keep it for a sunny November lunch before it closes for the winter.

name: Es Cantonet
village: Carrer de Gaspar Puig, Ibiza Town
open: Open all year · busy at lunch, book
desc: A proper neighbourhood restaurant a few streets from Dalt Vila where the locals eat: frita de pulpo, ensaladilla rusa, grilled vegetables and paella at prices that still make sense. No sea view, no concept — just home cooking and a full room.

name: Can Mimosa
open: Open all year · dinner Tue–Sat from 19:00, Sunday roast from 13:00
desc: A 200-year-old farmhouse tucked behind the square, run by Holly and Pedro: farmhouse cooking from island produce, a fireplace-and-garden kind of place, and the Sunday roast that half the island's expats plan their week around from October to May. They host private birthdays, anniversaries and office dinners of any size, tailored — email holly@canmimosaibiza.com.
ppp: Want it done for you? We'll set up your birthday or private table here — chef's menu, music, the guest list.

name: Can Sulayetas
open: Open all year from 10:00 · book, it fills
desc: A countryside bar on the Vénda de Rubió outside Sant Miquel that islanders have been driving to for years: a big terrace, dogs welcome, the parrillada as the house dish, sardines on Tuesdays, burgers on Thursdays, coconut flan to finish. €20–30 a head, 1,400 reviews and still nobody's secret but the locals'.
ppp: Want it done for you? We'll set up your birthday or private table here — chef's menu, music, the guest list.

name: Vino&Co
open: Open all year · Mon–Thu 10–14 & 17–20, Fri until 23:00, Sat mornings · closed Sunday
desc: The island's wine shop, with a tasting bar in the middle, a small terrace and a kitchen that does cheeses, jamón and pâtés to go with whatever is open. In winter the owners run tastings, workshops and Friday-night gatherings with special bites — the best-kept Friday on the island. Book a seat at the bar.
ppp: Want it done for you? We'll set up your birthday or private table here — chef's menu, music, the guest list.

name: Chidas Bar + Cantina
village: Plaça Pintor Vicent Calbet, Ibiza Town
open: Open all year from 17:00 · closed Sunday
desc: Modern Mexican taqueria and mezcal bar on a small square in town: tacos, tostadas, a long agave list and a late licence. Where the island's hospitality crowd ends up on a winter night. Watch for their Mezcal Monday collaborations.

name: Casa Lhasa
open: Open in winter · Mezcal Mondays from 18:00 — check Instagram for the week's hours
desc: A cosy village eatery in Sant Llorenç with a thing for mezcal: Monday nights are Mezcal Mondays — two-for-one tacos and snacks with Ojo de Isla cocktails, the artisanal mezcal made by an Ibiza-based founder, sometimes with a DJ. The kind of evening that makes a Monday in the north worth it.
ppp: Want it done for you? We'll set up your birthday or private table here — chef's menu, music, the guest list.

name: Casa Club
desc: Restaurant and bar in the centre of Santa Eulària that keeps its doors open and its music on all winter — dinners, drinks, live sessions and a crowd that lives here. Check their Instagram for this week's programme.
ppp: Want it done for you? We'll set up your birthday or private table here — chef's menu, music, the guest list.

name: Bodega Can Rich
open: Winter tours and tastings on weekdays · book ahead
desc: Organic winery on the Buscastell plain making the island's best-known wines, plus hierbas and olive oil. Guided tours of the vines and cellar end with a tasting — one of the few bodega visits that run right through the winter.

name: Bodega Sa Cova
desc: Family winery in the Sant Mateu valley, the island's wine country: a walk through the vines and the cellar, then a tasting paired with island cheeses and sobrassada. Combine with lunch at Ses Casetes on the square.

name: Bodegas Can Maymó
open: Shop open all year · tastings on request
desc: Small Sant Mateu bodega between the almond trees — reds, a rosé and a sweet wine sold straight from the finca. Buy a bottle, drink it on the terrace at sunset over the vineyards. In early December the whole valley celebrates the Festa del Vi Pagès with the new wine.

name: Ibizkus
open: Tours and tastings by appointment all year
desc: The island's most ambitious winery, on the Santa Eulària side of the island: guided visits of the production and tastings of their rosé and reds that make it onto restaurant lists across Europe. A good rainy-afternoon plan.

name: Salón San Miguel
open: Open in winter · check Instagram for days and hours
desc: A real Mexican salón on the hill by the fortified church of Sant Miquel — not tacos-for-tourists but the true thing, rooted in Mexican kitchen culture, with the aromas to match and the village at your feet. One of the most special tables in the north; book.
ppp: Want it done for you? We'll set up your birthday or private table here — chef's menu, music, the guest list.

name: SOMM Wine Shop
open: Open all year · tastings and pop-up dinners on request
desc: Swedish sommelier Anders Enkvist's shop in Santa Gertrudis, a 'talent scout for wines' since 2017: the island's own bottles, gin, beer, olive oil and hierbas next to serious finds from Italy, France and Austria. A tasting room for up to twenty — book a private tasting or a pop-up dinner for a winter night with friends.
ppp: Want it done for you? We'll set up your birthday or private table here — chef's menu, music, the guest list.

name: Ojo de Ibiza
open: Tasting room seasonal — 'see you next season'; wines in shops and restaurants all winter
desc: Dieter Meier's organic winery on twelve hectares of old terraces on the Pla de Sant Mateu, planted in 2015: the island's most polished bottles, made where the almond trees bloom in February. The tasting room by the vines closes for winter, but the wines are on the island's best lists and in SOMM and Vino&Co — drink them while you wait for spring.

name: Studiø Raffo
open: All winter · Color & Clay 14:00–17:00 on 30 Oct, 6–7 & 13–14 Nov, otherwise by appointment
desc: Cristina Raffo's ceramics studio in Cala Llonga: hand-built black stoneware and porcelain objects, one of a kind, and her Color & Clay afternoons where you paint your own pieces (€79, about 2.5 hours, groups of up to 6, everything fired and glazed for you). Private hand-building classes too. Write to book.

name: ERIDE Ibiza — electric retro motorcycles
open: All winter · tours and day rental, max 4 riders, book ahead
desc: A small independent outfit in Siesta renting retro-styled electric scramblers — real motorcycles, not scooters, silent and emission-free, up to 150 km on a charge. Golden Hour Ride (€85, 1.5–2 h): a guided loop timed to the best light of the day. Coast & Curves (€160, 3.5–4 h): the coast and the inland roads of the north with lunch and a drink. Day rental €120: morning pick-up, route suggestions, helmet and gloves, evening return. Groups of four at most. A car licence (B) with five years' experience is enough in Spain; any motorcycle licence works too.

name: Ibiza Ice Baths
desc: Mobile ice-bath service for the whole island: a luxury ice bath delivered to your villa, finca or holiday rental, set up and explained, from €200 a day (one-day minimum). Or book a guided session, about two hours, for yourself or a group — cold-therapy and breathwork coaches walk you in, from €499 depending on group size. November to March, on request. Book by WhatsApp.
